Prevention: Deep plough after harvesting to reduce crop residue
Brome grass and volunteer cereals during the dry season because they are alternative hosts of aphids
Synchronise planting date with low aphid populations by early planting at the onset of rains
Avoid moisture stress by using recommended varieties for the area and season, correct spacing and fertiliser rates and rotating with nitrogen fixing legumes such as beans and soyabean
Monitoring: Monitor frequently starting from seedling emergence in at least 4 locations in the field
Look for aphid colonies on young leaves or newly emerged flowers/ seed heads
Look for white to purple streaking on leaves and stems, leaf rolling, stunted plants and bleached heads (earliest infestation usually occurs at the edge of the field)
Spray chemicals when 5 aphids/ plant are observed at two leaf stage and 20 aphids/plant at booting stage
Direct Control: Spray with water during water stress periods
Hand pick colonies of aphids or remove heavily infested leaves and destroy by burning or burying
Seed dressing with thiamethoxam (Cruiser 70%WS) , Rate of application 150-250gm/100kg seed
Rate of application - during 'meher' season apply 1 g ai/ kg of seed and during 'Belg' season 1.5 g ai/kg of seed
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
